Bnay anasha, literally sons of man, is the generic human-being expression here; people renders that lexicalized construct rather than asserting literal sons.

Men l-gaw is the compound interior-location adverb, literally from within. In this description of the false prophets inward nature it means inwardly; men contributes to that adverb rather than a separate origin complement. The following adversative deyn at position 10 is linked separately.

Men mtum is the temporal idiom from ever/at any time, here governed by the separately linked negative at position 5. Its English adverb ever renders the compound; the relative prefix on position 3 independently owns that earlier in the clause.
